contact_edits.before: Salt-Water Moon is a slighter play than Leaving Home, but it's also more likeable and has fewer loose ends. Its principal weakness is that though we hear, evocatively, about the decline of the local fisheries and, less evocatively, about the shadowing trauma of the recent war, neither theme seems to have entered into the blood and being of the couple we actually see. It's background, part of the "this is our country, look at it" aesthetic that underlies most of French's plays, not to mention others of the time, such as David Fennario's Balconville. It was probably a necessary phase for Canadian drama to pass through, but it's difficult to imagine the plays being taken as seriously anywhere else. But here is here, and the plays have cut a distinctive new panel in Soulpepper's tapestry. A company whose repertory roams the world needs to come home now and then. - Salt-Water Moon runs until Jan. 31. Call 416-866-8666 for more information.
